<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par145 />{{GHGmargin-letter|145|k}}
'''4.''' Plurals of names of animals or things, and of abstracts, whether they be masculine or feminine, are frequently construed with the feminine singular of the verbal predicate<ref>Cf. in Greek the construction of the neuter plural with the singular of the predicate τὰ πρόβατα βαίνει; in Attic Greek the plural of the predicate is allowed only when the neuter denotes actual persons, as τὰ ἀνδράποδα ἔλαβον. In Arabic also the ''pluralis inhumanus'' (i.e. not denoting persons) is regularly construed with the feminine singular of the attribute or predicate, as are all the ''plurales fracti'' (properly collective forms).</ref> (on the collective sense of the feminine form, cf. {{GHGpar|122|s}}); thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֲמוֹת שָׂדֶה תַּֽעֲרֹג|translate=the beasts of the field long}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=12|verse=4}} (where the predicate precedes), cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=7}}; names of things with the predicate preceding occur in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=34|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=51|verse=29|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=35}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=31|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=2|hidebook=1}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, 103:5 (unless {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמְחַדֵּשׁ}} is to be read for {{GHGheb|text=תִּתְחַדֵּשׁ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=19}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=27|verse=20|hidebook=1}}; with the predicate following, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=49|verse=22}} ({{GHGheb|text=בָּנוֹת}}=''branches''); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=4|verse=15}} ({{GHGheb|text=וְעֵינָיו קָ֫מָה}}),<ref>On the possibility of explaining forms like {{GHGheb|text=קָ֫מָה}} as 3rd plural feminine, cf. above, {{GHGpar|44|m}}; but this explanation would not apply to all the cases under this head, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jo|chapter=1|verse=20}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=37|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=5|hidebook=1}}.</ref> {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=10|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=59|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=15}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}, 48:41, 49:24, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=15|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=18|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=10}}.<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=1}} an abstract plural {{GHGheb|text=חָכְמוֹת}} (to be read thus with 9:1, &c., instead of {{GHGheb|text=חַכְמוֹת}}) is construed with the singular; but cf. {{GHGpar|86|l}}, {{GHGpar|124|e}}, end.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|l}}
'''5.''' Moreover, the plural of persons (especially in the participle) is sometimes construed with the singular of the predicate, when instead of the whole class of individuals, each severally is to be represented as affected by the statement. Undoubted examples of this ''distributive'' singular are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=29}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=9}}) {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽרֲרֶ֫יךָ אָרוּר וּמְבָֽרֲכֶ֫יךָ בָּרוּךְ|translate=those that curse thee, cursed be}} every one of them, ''and those that bless thee, blessed be'' every one of them; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=31|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=17|verse=14}} and 19:8 (in both places the Samaritan has {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽכְלוֹ}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=12}} unless {{GHGheb|text=נֽׄגְשָׂיו}} is to be regarded as a ''pluralis maiestatis'' according to {{GHGpar|124|k}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=3|verse=18.35}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=18|verse=21|hidebook=1}} (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=21|verse=27b|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=16|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=28|verse=1b|hidebook=1}}, 28:16 {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|145|m}}
Rem. Analogous to the examples above mentioned is the somewhat frequent<ref>In several of the above examples the text is doubtful, and hence Mayer Lambert ({{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} xxiv. 110) rejects the theory of distributive singulars generally. [Cf. Driver, ''Jeremiah'', p. 362, on 16:7.]</ref> use of suffixes in the singular (distributively) referring to plurals; cf. the {{GHGterm|verbal}}-suffixes in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=21|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=28|verse=48|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=6|verse=10}}; and the ''noun''-suffixes in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=22|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=14}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=4|verse=8}} (but since {{GHGheb|text=ו}} follows, {{GHGheb|text=נַפְשׁוֹ}} is undoubtedly a dittography for {{GHGheb|text=נָֽפֶשׁ}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=5|verse=10}} (where, however, {{GHGheb|text=פִּימוֹ}} is clearly to be read with all the early versions); 62:5, 141:10 (?), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=38|verse=32}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=10|verse=15}} [but LXX {{GHGheb|text=הַכְּסִיל}}]; finally, the suffixes with prepositions in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=2|verse=20}} {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר עָֽשׂוּ־לוֹ|translate=which they made}} each one ''for himself'' (according to others, ''which they'' (''the makers'') ''made for him''); 5:26, 8:20, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=5}}, in each case {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ}}; in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=19}} {{GHGheb|text=לוֹ}} refers to the collectives {{GHGheb|text=חַיָּה}} and {{GHGheb|text=עוֹף}}; cf. further, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=24|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=5|verse=23}} {{GHGheb|text=מִמֶּ֫נּוּ}} after {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיקִים}} (but read probably {{GHGheb|text=צַדִּיק}} with the LXX, &c.). Conversely in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=1|verse=11}} {{GHGheb|text=עִבְרִי לָכֶם}} [cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=13|verse=20}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>th.}}], but the text is undoubtedly corrupt.
